_about: RT-4 class A: seven served draft turns (red-team #87 5998705341), replayed at 0 LLM. Briefs are the red team’s synthetic briefs. draft_graph and the served manifest verdicts are verbatim from the wire.

briefs.bakery: We run a chain of 14 independent bakeries across Leeds and York. Wholesale flour costs rose 18% this year and our gross margin fell from 62% to 54%. We are weighing three options: (A) raise bread prices by 8% in every shop; (B) close our two weakest shops, which lose about £40k a year each, and consolidate baking in a central kitchen that would cost £250k to fit out; or (C) launch a wholesale subscription for local cafés, targeting 60 cafés at £300 a month. Our goal is to get gross margin back above 60% within 12 months without cutting staff hours. We think an 8% price rise would cut footfall by about 5%, and a central kitchen would cut waste from 12% of output to 6%.
briefs.support: Our support team handles 12,000 tickets a month with 30 agents. Median first response is 9 hours, and customers who wait more than a day churn at 4% a month against 1.5% for everyone else. We are choosing between hiring 10 more agents at £38k each a year, buying an AI triage tool for £120k a year that the vendor says deflects 35% of tickets, or doing nothing. Our goal is to get monthly churn below 2% within 9 months. Our head of support thinks the tool will deflect only 15% of tickets, not 35%.
briefs.consultancy: We are a 25-person software consultancy with annual gross profit of £1.1m. We are choosing between three options: hire 3 senior consultants at £95k each, launch a fixed-price security audit product at £8k per audit aiming for 40 audits a year, or raise our day rate from £900 to £1,000. Our goal is to grow annual gross profit above £1.4m within 12 months. Each senior consultant should bill about 150 days a year. We think raising the day rate by about 10% would cost us around 5% of our billable days.
briefs.brief3: We're a 40-person architecture practice deciding whether to open a second office in Manchester or put the money into overhauling our BIM software and training instead. The partners are split on it. What we want is more profitable work over the next two years.
